headword: {寒中見舞|かんちゅうみま}い

definitions.explanation: A seasonal greeting, usually a postcard, sent during the coldest part of the year (from about January 8 to early February) to ask after someone's health. It also takes the place of a New Year's card when either side is in mourning, and is used to answer New Year's cards that arrived too late to reply to in time.

examples.japanese: {寒中見舞|かんちゅうみま}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{寒中見舞|かんちゅうみま}い⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}いた→届く：00899_todoku⟧。
examples.english: A midwinter greeting card arrived from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: ⟦{喪中|もちゅう}→喪中：06226_mochuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代|か}わり→代わり：01296_kawari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{寒中見舞|かんちゅうみま}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}ります→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: To people in mourning, we send a midwinter greeting instead of a New Year card.

notes:
The card usually opens with the set phrase {寒中|かんちゅう}⟦お{見舞|みま}い→お見舞い：01351_omimai⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧ ("wishing you well in this cold season"). Because New Year's cards are not sent to or by families in mourning (⟦{喪中|もちゅう}→喪中：06226_mochuu⟧), the midwinter card takes their place.
